channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold: Safe-haven bid on US debt worries – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes Gold has surged, breaking above USD 4,500 per troy ounce as safe‑haven demand rises on US debt concerns and a weaker Dollar.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Neutral RSI signals further consolidation
item.description: EUR/GBP remains stuck in a narrow trading range this month, stalling the rebound from near 0.8460 in mid-July as buyers struggle to clear the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA).

item.title: British Pound dips hold above 216.50 Japanese Yen following mixed UK data
item.description: British Pound's (GBP) rally against the Japanese Yen (JPY) was capped at the 217.00 area earlier on Friday, and the pair pulled back to the 216.50 area where it found some support.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Binary tariff risks shape near-term path – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that Section 338 tariff negotiations pose a binary risk for the Canadian Dollar (CAD) and USD/CAD.

item.title: Silver climbs toward $70 as US Dollar remains under pressure
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) accelerates its advance on Friday and trades around $69.75 at the time of writing, up 2.41% on the day. The white metal reaches its highest level in two months and is on track for a weekly gain of more than 7%, mainly supported by persistent weakness in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro: Set to outperform Pound, US Dollar and Yen - Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists see greater fiscal vulnerabilities in the United Kingdom (UK) than in the Euro area. Strong foreign inflows into Euro area bonds and comparatively better debt dynamics support its view that Euro (EUR) should outperform British Pound (GBP), US Dollar (USD) and Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Indian Rupee remains under pressure amid elevated Oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) ticks lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR edges up to near 95.72 as elevated oil prices have outweighed a weak US Dollar.

item.title: Australian Dollar rallies above 0.7150 as the US Dollar bleeds amid bond buybacks
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) accelerated its rally against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, hitting session highs above 0.7150 for the first time since early June and drawing closer to a three-month top, in the 0.7200 area.

item.title: Experts agree: Weak Dollar backs near-term upside in EUR/USD
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades 0.21% higher at around 1.1710 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday, the highest level seen in over three months.

item.title: US Dollar: Yield management weighs on currency – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is weaker against all major currencies as longer-term US Treasury yields edge lower following buyback plans. Haddad argues expanded buybacks and fiscal messaging may cap long-end yields but at a credibility cost for the USD.

item.title: $4,600: Gold rallies to three-month high, eyes third weekly gain
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) is heading for a third consecutive weekly gain on Friday, extending an impressive rally that has lifted the precious metal by around 13% so far this month. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades near $4,590 after briefly climbing above $4,600, its highest level since May 15.

item.title: US Dollar broadly consolidates as analysts cast doubts over long-term impact of US Treasury buyback
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is broadly consolidating near the 99.00 level as investors process the US Treasury's expanded long-end bond buyback and a modest rebound in Treasury yields.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar climbs to highest since June as US Dollar weakens
item.description: NZD/USD extends its advance on Friday and trades around 0.5980 at the time of writing, up 0.62% on the day. The pair reached its highest level since early June and is heading for a solid weekly performance, mainly supported by persistent weakness in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD testing three-month highs near $4,600 as the US Dollar dives
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends gains on Friday, with bulls aiming for a retest of the $4,600 resistance area, the top of the last six months' trading range.

item.title: US Dollar: Limited upside as fiscal plans questioned – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that the US Dollar has weakened as investors focus on potential US Treasury measures to stem the decline in Treasury yields, while Japanese inflation data supports expectations for a 25bp BoJ rate hike in September.

item.title: United Kingdom: Burnham sentiment bounce – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a sharp improvement in sentiment towards Prime Minister Burnham and Labour.

item.title: S&P Global US PMIs expected to ease slightly in August, still showing solid growth
item.description: S&P Global will release the preliminary figures of August’s United States Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs), a report collecting top private sector executives' opinions about business conditions, to provide an early indication of momentum in the world’s largest economy.

item.title: United States: Yields risk renewed surge – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior US Strategist Philip Marey discusses United States (US) Treasuries, noting that the Treasury Department’s surprise move to boost buybacks of longer-term bonds has only briefly interrupted rising yields.

item.title: 1.3670: British Pound hits six-month highs as UK PMI beats expectations
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) rallied to fresh six-month highs against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, boosted by stronger-than-expected UK business activity data, while the US Dollar remains depressed following the US Treasury’s plan to boost bond buybacks.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $69.94 per troy ounce, up 2.67% from the $68.12 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank keeps tightening option open – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke reports that the Riksbank left its policy rate at 1.75% and maintained a restrictive stance, still seeing a hike later this year as likely.

item.title: ECB’s Kazāks: Central bank is well placed to act if needed to get inflation to 2%
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Mārtiņš Kazāks said during the European trading session on Friday that the central bank won’t hesitate to act if needed to bring Eurozone inflationary pressures down to the 2% target.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness offsets intervention impact – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Michael Wan notes that US longer-end yields have returned close to pre-buyback levels, with the 10-year at 4.7% and 30-year at 5.24%, weighing on risk assets.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Oil supply tightness supports further upside above $90
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade flat near $86.00 during the European trading session on Friday, closer to its over three-week high of $87.38 posted the previous day.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer bias with pro-risk flows – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner, Francesco Pesole and Frantisek Taborsky argue that recent US Treasury buy-backs are primarily a signalling tool against high yields, pointing to a softer Dollar in a risk-friendly environment.

item.title: Gold rallies to its highest level since late May, eyes $4,600 on weak USD ahead of US PMIs
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) builds on the intraday breakout momentum above a technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) and climbs to its highest level since late May during the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Euro steadies against British Pound as strong PMIs offer support on both sides
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8570 on Friday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen sticks to gains amid hawkish BoJ bets as USD stays weak on Fed expectations
item.description: The USD/JPY pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's recovery from the 158.00 mark, or a one-and-a-half-week low, and meets with fresh supply on Friday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Backstop doubts and high intervention bar – BNY
item.description: BNY’s David Tam stresses that while the Federal Reserve retains legal capacity to support corporate credit, the current Warsh Fed is unlikely to repeat Covid‑era interventions.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Inflation re-acceleration weighs on PLN – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose highlights growing challenges for Polish policymakers, citing stretched fiscal plans and accelerating underlying inflation.
